# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c3 P1](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0001)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a short, fat, and bald man with a round face and prominent blue eyes. When enraged, his face turns purple and his eyes stick out. After reuniting with his wife, he dresses in a remarkably neat and snug manner.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Personality

Harrison is an eccentric, outspoken, and fidgety man who prides himself on his blunt frankness. Although outwardly crusty, crabbed, and cantankerous, he is deep down a kind and sympathetic neighbor. He dislikes being pitied, smokes a pipe, and is hard to please regarding literary matters, offering candid and unvarnished criticism.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c6 P56](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0056), [v2 c9 P40](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0040), [v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039)_

## Goals

- To live in peace without excessive housecleaning and nagging  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>

## History

Mr. J. A. Harrison originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick. After his sister died, he married Emily Scott to fulfill a deathbed promise, but the two separated over household friction and her hatred of his parrot, Ginger. Harrison subsequently moved to Prince Edward Island and purchased Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea. Initially viewed as an eccentric bickering crank by the community, he hired John Henry Carter and lived a bachelor's life. He eventually formed a warm friendship with his young neighbor, Anne Shirley. Later, his wife Emily arrived in Avonlea and reconciled with him following Ginger's death. Following his reunion with Emily, Harrison became a regular churchgoer who subscribed to the minister's salary, growing increasingly sociable and well-regarded in the community.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059), [v2 c27 P9](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0009), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Background by volume

- Lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick before moving to Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- Promised his late sister on her deathbed that he would marry Emily Scott  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Separated from his wife Emily due to bickering over neatness, grammar, and his late brother's swearing parrot  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Kept a parrot named Ginger given to him by his dying brother  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea adjoining the Cuthbert place  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> That old nuisance of a Rachel Lynde was here again today, pestering me for a subscription towards buying a carpet for the vestry room. I detest that woman more than anybody I know. She can put a whole sermon, text, comment, and application, into six words, and throw it at you like a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> I don’t believe in putting marrying off too long—like I did.  <sub>[v3 c12 P76](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0076)</sub>
